page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.14xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the KVM hypervisor. It runs on the x86_64 architecture and is driven by dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processors operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The instance provisions 56 virtual CPUs across 28 physical cores with two threads per core, supported by 35 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 224.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. This configuration does not include local storage or dedicated hardware GPU accelerators, while network throughput is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

Benchmark results reflect the multi-threaded capabilities and single-thread limitations of the older Broadwell architecture. In parallel execution, the server achieves middle-tier results, demonstrated by an average multi-core stress-ng rating of 40,954.08, a Geekbench multi-core score of 9,467.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 35,028.65. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 104.82 GB/sec. Conversely, per-core performance sits in the lower tier, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 948.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 19.05 GB/sec, which falls into the bottom ten percent.

From an efficiency standpoint, the ecs.sn2ne.14xlarge provides high core density and balanced memory allocation suited for horizontally scaled systems, though legacy microarchitecture yields lower throughput per cycle compared to newer generation processors. Given the absence of local disks, storage operations rely entirely on network-attached block volumes. This server profile fits multi-threaded web serving, enterprise resource planning backends, static asset delivery, and distributed data processing pipelines that do not depend on high single-thread clock speeds.

Operating on the x86_64 architecture under KVM virtualization, it provides a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation, a 10 Gbps baseline network interface, zero bundled local storage, and no GPU acceleration. Benchmark profiles indicate solid multi-core throughput alongside weaker single-core processing metrics typical of legacy Intel Xeon architectures. The server handles large multi-threaded workloads, distributed application backends, batch processing, and horizontally scaled web services effectively, provided tasks do not require extreme single-thread performance or onboard NVMe storage.
